items.description: Ranomafana is a lush rainforest park famous for its golden bamboo lemurs and hot springs.
The Masoala Peninsula contains the largest area of protected rainforest in Madagascar, meeting the sea in a stunning way.
Lake Tampolo is a serene coastal lake on the east coast, surrounded by rare littoral forest.
The coast around Mahajanga features massive estuaries and beautiful red-rock formations.
Sainte Marie (Nosy Boraha) is a tropical island paradise known for whale watching and its pirate history.
The Tsiribihina Delta is a vast wetland area where the river meets the Mozambique Channel.
Lake Tsimanampetsotsa is a saline lake in the dry south, famous for its blind cave fish and flamingos.
The Mangoro River is one of Madagascar's longest rivers, vital for transport and hydroelectric power.
Nosy Mitsio is a stunning archipelago of volcanic islands with unique rock formations and clear waters.
Montagne d'Ambre is a volcanic mountain park in the north, known for its waterfalls and cool climate.
Lake Anivorano is a sacred lake in northern Madagascar, home to crocodiles that are respected by the local people.
Nosy Tanikely is a small island reserve offering some of the best snorkeling in the Nosy Be region.
The Makay Massif is a remote and rugged sandstone labyrinth, one of the least explored areas of Madagascar.
The foothills of Boby Peak lead to the highest climbable summit in Madagascar, set within Andringitra National Park.
The Manongarivo Massif is an isolated mountain range in the north, protecting a vast area of primary forest.
Vohimana is a mountainous region in the eastern rainforest, known for its steep slopes and rich biodiversity.
The rolling hills of Ranomafana are covered in dense rainforest, providing a dramatic backdrop to the park.
